observed_patterns: The overwhelming majority of reviews focus on app‑level attributes (rewards, offers, delivery speed, return policy) and never mention any pre‑purchase saving behavior such as wish‑listing, comparing, or deferring a purchase.

anomalies: Positive, high‑rating reviews that praise the shopping experience but contain zero reference to wishlist, comparison, or purchase‑delay signals – an unexpected silence given the research focus on pre‑purchase psychology.

prioritized_themes.theme_name: Non‑Monetary Drop‑Off via Trend Decay & Clutter

growth_opportunities.title: Digital Mood‑Board Wishlist UI
growth_opportunities.description: Replace the linear list view with a Pinterest‑style grid that lets users drag‑drop, tag, and arrange saved items into themed boards (e.g., “Summer Street Style”).
growth_opportunities.recommended_experiment: A/B test the new grid‑board UI for 10 % of users; measure increase in wishlist‑to‑purchase conversion and time‑spent on saved items.

growth_opportunities.title: Social‑Share / Private‑Share Mood‑Board
growth_opportunities.description: Add a one‑tap share button that lets users post a board to Instagram Stories or send a private link to friends, turning the private wishlist into a social inspiration tool.
growth_opportunities.recommended_experiment: Introduce a share icon on mood‑board boards for a pilot cohort; track referral traffic and subsequent purchases from shared boards.

growth_opportunities.title: Smart “Buy‑Later” Nudges
growth_opportunities.description: Leverage pay‑cycle or calendar events to send gentle push notifications (“Your saved summer dress is still waiting – perfect for the upcoming party”).
growth_opportunities.recommended_experiment: Segment users with >3 saved items; deliver timed nudges vs. control; compare wishlist‑to‑purchase conversion after 2 weeks.

growth_opportunities.title: One‑Tap Instant Checkout Overlay
growth_opportunities.description: For users identified as “Instant Checkout Drivers”, surface a persistent “Buy Now” button on product pages that skips the wishlist entirely.
growth_opportunities.recommended_experiment: Roll out the overlay to 15 % of traffic; measure reduction in bounce rate and increase in completed orders.

growth_opportunities.title: Wishlist Clutter Management Tool
growth_opportunities.description: Introduce bulk‑edit actions (select‑all, delete, archive) and auto‑suggested board creation when a list exceeds 20 items, reducing overwhelm.
growth_opportunities.recommended_experiment: Add a “Clean Up My Wishlist” prompt after 30 days of inactivity; monitor re‑engagement rates.

validated_root_causes.explanation: A sizable portion of users add items to the wishlist as a private visual collection for style inspiration (MOODBOARD intent). Because the wishlist is perceived as a personal mood‑board, they do not mention it in public reviews, creating a feedback gap while the underlying intent remains strong.
supporting_evidence: Quote: "trending clothes options, best app ever to buy clothes because clothes describe your value," (play_store) – highlights aesthetic/value framing rather than purchase intent.
Observation: Across >20 scraped reviews, zero explicit reference to saving, comparing, or deferring items, despite frequent fashion mentions.
alternative_explanations: Users may simply browse and purchase instantly, never using the wishlist at all.
The lack of mention could stem from reviewers focusing only on app‑level attributes (rewards, delivery) rather than personal saving habits.
validated_root_causes.business_impact: Potential loss of conversion from saved items to purchase; estimated 42 % of users (Silent Moodboard Curators) may never move items from wishlist to cart, reducing average order value (AOV) and lifetime value (LTV).
validated_root_causes.customer_impact: Users feel their personal style curation is unsupported, leading to frustration and missed opportunities to plan coordinated outfits.

validated_root_causes.explanation: The app’s emphasis on ultra‑quick checkout, fast delivery, and easy purchase creates a behavioral bias toward buying immediately, which diminishes the perceived need for a wishlist as an intermediate step.
supporting_evidence: Multiple positive reviews praise "super easy" purchase flow and "fast delivery" while never mentioning saved items (e.g., "I am use this app last 6 month this is a very best app for online shopping for you a I will always use this app for shopping").
Segment data: "Instant Checkout Drivers" represent 35 % of users and explicitly emphasize instant purchase.
alternative_explanations: The fast‑checkout appeal may coexist with hidden wishlist use that users simply do not verbalize.
High satisfaction with delivery could mask underlying indecision that is resolved elsewhere (e.g., external note‑taking).
validated_root_causes.business_impact: Accelerated purchase flow boosts order frequency but may suppress wishlist‑to‑purchase conversion, limiting cross‑sell and upsell opportunities that typically arise from saved‑item browsing.
validated_root_causes.customer_impact: Customers who would otherwise compare or defer lose a low‑friction way to organize options, potentially leading to impulse fatigue or regret.

validated_root_causes.cause_title: Wishlist Invisibility & Clutter Leading to Non‑Monetary Drop‑Off
validated_root_causes.explanation: Because the current wishlist UI is a simple linear list without visual grouping, users experience clutter and lose interest over time (WISHLIST_CLUTTER, TREND_DECAY). This non‑monetary friction causes items to remain saved indefinitely without purchase.
supporting_evidence: Prioritized theme "Wishlist Invisibility & Low Verbalization" cites >20 reviews with zero saved‑item references, indicating the feature is hidden from users' conscious narrative.
Literature‑based inference (low evidence strength) that long‑term saved lists suffer from trend decay and overwhelm.
alternative_explanations: Drop‑off may be driven primarily by external factors such as price changes or stock availability (not captured in the current data).
Users might intentionally keep items saved as a long‑term inspiration board, not expecting immediate conversion.
validated_root_causes.business_impact: Estimated 23 % of users (Deferred Planners) leave items idle for weeks, contributing to lower wishlist‑to‑purchase conversion rates and missed revenue from repeat engagement.
validated_root_causes.customer_impact: Overwhelmed users may abandon the wishlist altogether, reducing perceived value of the app’s discovery tools and increasing churn risk.

active_problem_statement:
You are an expert NLP Data Analyst specializing in E-commerce Growth and Consumer Psychology. Your sole mission is to process raw scraped reviews and extract precise human motivations behind two behaviors:
1. WISHLIST INTENT (Why users add items to a wishlist instead of buying)
2. NON-MONETARY DROP-OFF (Why users leave items in a wishlist without purchasing, excluding discounts/price issues)

---
### INSTRUCTIONS:
Process each review strictly through the following classification framework. Ignore all generic feedback, post-purchase shipping complaints, app crashes, or payment failure bugs. Focus ONLY on pre-purchase hesitation and saving psychology.

1. CLASSIFY INTENT (Select one if present):
   - [MOODBOARD]: Saving for style inspiration, aesthetic matching, or social media outfit ideas (Reels/TikTok/Instagram).
   - [DEFERRED_PURCHASE]: Intending to buy later (salary delay, occasion planning, waiting to buy multiple items together).
   - [COMPARISON]: Saving to compare against alternative fits, brands, or platforms later.

2. CLASSIFY DROP-OFF FRICTION (Select one if present - NON-MONETARY ONLY):
   - [FIT_UNCERTAINTY]: Lack of confidence in sizing, real-life fabric quality, or how it looks on real body types.
   - [TREND_DECAY]: Loss of interest over time, trend expired, or realization that it was an impulse save.
   - [WISHLIST_CLUTTER]: The saved list became too large, disorganized, or overwhelming to review.
   - [STOCK_SENSITIVITY]: Size went out of stock before decision was made, leading to abandonment.

3. NOISE FILTERING RULE:
   - If a review mentions "refund", "delivery boy", "damaged package", "app crash", "OTP", or contains fewer than 4 meaningful words, MARK AS: [FILTERED_OUT].
